title: Correct the measurement-basis record and its worked examples after the owner's reviewer's check: every example describes a building that fits and the test checks the fit; the estimate's formula; shared floor area as a required step; the amenity base; the eligibility of the energy and wall exclusions; unequal floors; the open points hold only the owner's choices (backlog rows DB-177, DB-178; D-090 R435, R436, R509 to R516, R519, R532, R534)
objective: CORRECT THE MEASUREMENT-BASIS RECORD AND ITS WORKED EXAMPLES after the check by the owner's reviewer (project-control/directives/D-090-product-plan-2026-09-28-start-building/source-055-amendment.md, 'A needs the following corrections before implementation'; docs/DISCOVERY_BACKLOG.md rows DB-177 and DB-178). No estimator is built and no program code changes; the only code is the examples' own test files. (A) EVERY EXAMPLE DESCRIBES A BUILDING THAT FITS. Confirmed from the files: in Example C the schedule lists, per upper floor, 1,120 sq ft of apartment rooms (28 x 40, the whole stated inside outline) and then partitions, demising walls, the exterior wall ring, a corridor, a stair, an elevator and chases, 1,743 sq ft in all, against a stated outside outline of 30 x 42 = 1,260 sq ft; its ground floor has no stated outline. Example B states no floor outline at all (an 'outer ring proxy' stands for the walls). Example A adds up to its 40 x 50 floor. THE RULE: every floor of every example has a stated outside outline (rectangles with their dimensions), and the components listed on that floor, the exterior wall ring among them, add up to exactly the area of that outline; every component says on which floors it lies. Examples B and C are rebuilt to that rule with every dimension stated; Example A gains the per-floor statement. The JSON form is the builder's to extend (for example a list of floors, each with its outline and its components), kept simple; the Markdown files are regenerated by the existing renderer. The ratios of B and C change as a consequence: each example's change log and the record say which figures were withdrawn (0.6022 and 0.6676) and why; nothing is replaced silently. (B) THE TEST CHECKS THE FIT (R511). The examples' test fails when the components of a floor do not add up to that floor's outline, when a floor has no outline, and when the rooms fill the inside outline and other inside components are listed on top. RED PROOF, in this order: the new check is written first and run against the examples as they are at the claim head; it fails for Example C and for Example B; that output goes into the report; only then are the examples repaired. (C) THE RECORD (`docs/measurement-basis/MEASUREMENT_BASIS.md`). (C1) THE FORMULA, stated once, in words: the estimated number of apartments is the PROPOSED BUILDING'S residential zoning floor area, times an assumed apartment-area ratio, divided by an assumed apartment size measured as HPD measures it. The maximum permitted floor area is a separate figure, a limit to check the proposal against, never the area the estimate starts from. Where a layout measures the apartments themselves, that measured area is used directly in place of floor area times ratio. No count is computed in the record. (C2) THE RANGE: the examples establish no range; 0.60 to 0.75, if the owner adopts it, is a chosen sensitivity range labelled unvalidated; no sentence calls it realistic, expected or validated. (C3) SHARED FLOOR AREA IN A BUILDING WITH MORE THAN ONE USE IS A REQUIRED STEP, not a choice and not a switch: the record quotes the sentence of the capture `zr-23-20` ('Where #floor area# in a #building# is shared by multiple #uses# ...') with its capture id and digest, says in plain words what it requires, says that it does not necessarily raise the residential figure, and says what is not settled: the section the reviewer names for mixed buildings (ZR 35-31) is captured by task M4-T034 of this same wave and is NOT read here, so how a mixed building in a commercial district combines its floor areas is withheld until that text is captured and read. Where the areas the attribution needs are missing, the result that depends on it is 'not known' or explicitly conditional. Example C marks every component as exclusive to one use or shared, carries the attribution as a line of its reconciliation, and, if it has shared floor area, applies the attribution exactly as the captured sentence words it and labels the outcome conditional on the text not yet read. (C4) THE AMENITY RULE: the capture `zr-23-231` names the base of its 5 percent, 'the residential floor area of the building'; it covers eligible amenity space actually provided and accessible to residents; circulation is not amenity space; it is never an automatic 5 percent added to apartment space. Open point 5 no longer asks the owner what the base is; a remaining doubt about the ORDER of calculation, if the builder finds one in the captured words, goes under the questions of law with 'not sure' and the link. (C5) THE ENERGY AND WALL EXCLUSIONS HAVE SPECIFIC ELIGIBILITY: the record quotes the capture `zr-12-10-qualifying-exterior-wall-thickness` (thickness added to a building existing on December 6, 2023; over-cladding and re-cladding) and says it is not a deduction for the walls of a new building; for the energy exclusion it quotes the sentence of `zr-12-10-floor-area` and says that the two definitions it rests on ('fully electrified building', 'ultra low energy building') are captured by task M4-T034 and not read here, so the exclusion's eligibility is withheld and no example takes it. A user's statement supports only a conditional result; it never establishes eligibility. No sentence offers a general 'confirm it applies' choice. (C6) UNEQUAL FLOORS: the section on how an assumption changes the count says that the floors above the maximum base height are set back and are smaller than the floors below, so a count of floors times one floorplate is an assumption and is labelled as one; it quotes the captured table of ZR 23-432 for the district's base and building heights and the capture of ZR 23-433 for the setback, and says the program does not work out the setback yet. (C7) SECTION 8 IS REWRITTEN INTO TWO LISTS. 'Choices for the owner' holds only design assumptions and what is displayed: the ratio (one figure, or a low and a high as a sensitivity range labelled unvalidated); the apartment size (700 sq ft as a chosen starting assumption on the HPD basis); the floor heights (10 ft and 15 ft as editable starting assumptions subject to the actual building envelope); 'not known' until an option has a shape and floors, and after that the name 'preliminary capacity estimate'. Each carries the line: recommended by the owner's reviewer on 2026-10-07; NOT decided until the owner says so. 'Questions of law' holds what is resolved by capturing and reading the text, never by preference (R515), each with what is captured, what is not, and 'not sure' where the text leaves doubt. The former points 5, 6 and 7 move there. EVERY STATEMENT OF LAW QUOTES A CAPTURE that exists under docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/ at the claim head, with its id and digest, read by the builder from the capture file; a statement that would need a text not captured is written as 'not captured yet' and never from memory or from the reviewer's message. The standing label (a draft reading by an AI, not professionally reviewed) stays. NOT IN THIS TASK: an estimator; any starting value approved; any file outside the two folders; any capture; any reference case.
business_reason: The owner's reviewer would not approve the measurement-basis package as written: one worked example describes a building that does not fit while its arithmetic passes; a required step of the law was offered as a switch; two questions of law were put to the owner as preferences. The record is what the owner is asked to decide on, so it is corrected before it is put to the owner again and before any estimator (R531, R534).
